Guillermo's own take for Fri, Nov 13 (his read, quote it as his, not yours): Howe Sound outflow is peaking right now, with Pam Rocks at N 22 at 7am and climbing, and EC has a gale warning out. Porteau works if you're already rolling, but EC has it dying to light later this morning. 

Sand Heads is already ESE 14 to 21 and EC calls SE 20 to 30 by early afternoon, stronger than the page. Boundary Bay runs from about noon to last light around 5, and the tide stays above 10ft all. 

Check before driving: if Sand Heads reads SE 15 plus at noon, go.

EC marine forecast, Howe Sound (issued 04:00 AM PCT 13 November 2026), WARNING IN EFFECT: Today Tonight and Saturday. Gale warning in effect. Wind northerly outflow 25 to 35 knots diminishing to light this morning then increasing to southerly inflow 5 to 15 Saturday morning. Wind becoming northerly outflow 10 to 20 Saturday evening. Strong wind warning program has ended for the season.

EC marine forecast, Strait of Georgia (south of Nanaimo) (issued 04:00 AM PCT 13 November 2026), WARNING IN EFFECT: Today Tonight and Saturday. Gale warning in effect. Wind southeast 5 to 15 knots backing to east 15 to 20 early this morning then increasing to southeast 20 to 30 early this afternoon. Wind diminishing to southeast 15 to 20 early this evening then increasing to southeast 25 Saturday afternoon. Wind increasing to southeast 25 to 35 Saturday evening. Strong wind warning program has ended for the season.
